insights.topic: Verified purchase proof vs. probabilistic targeting
insights.insight: Crinkl has confirmed $2.17M in beta GMV across 37,576+ receipts using cryptographic receipt verification — each record is a confirmed transaction, not an inferred intent signal. For CMOs evaluating cookieless alternatives, this is the structural distinction: deterministic purchase proof at scale versus audience modeling built on behavioral proxies.

The 14-day window shows grocery-supermarkets leading volume (1,312 receipts, ~$61 average basket) while an unclassified 'Unknown' category posts a ~$336 average basket — roughly 5.5x grocery — indicating high-ticket verified spend is present and not yet attributed to a brand or channel. Marketers chasing premium-buyer segments should note this unresolved category as a signal worth watching as classification matures.

insights.topic: Digital and subscription commerce confirmed in verified receipt set
insights.insight: YouTube appearing in the top brand list alongside Amazon, OpenAI, Stripe, Paddle, Gumroad, and Suno confirms the receipt verification layer captures digital purchases and SaaS subscriptions — not just physical retail. This expands the addressable use case beyond CPG and grocery into subscription retention, digital upsell, and cross-category attribution.

insights.topic: Home improvement emerging as a category signal
insights.insight: The Home Depot (67 receipts, 14-day) and Lowe's both appear in the top brand list simultaneously — the most concentrated brand-list expansion recorded in the monitoring window. Two competing home improvement brands crossing the visibility threshold in the same heartbeat sequence is a category-level signal, not a coincidence, and warrants attention from brands targeting homeowner segments.

insights.topic: Rolling-window GMV is a mechanical artifact, not a demand read
insights.insight: Seven consecutive UTC midnight rollovers have each produced sharp apparent GMV drops — as much as $171K to $109K in a single boundary crossing — that fully recover within 4–16 hours. CMOs evaluating platform health metrics should treat any rolling-window GMV figure in isolation as structurally misleading; the underlying receipt cadence of ~360–380 per day has held without acceleration or decay across the full monitoring window.

insights.topic: Stable reward policy signals operational discipline
insights.insight: The sats-per-receipt rate has held at 129 without change across the full monitoring window, even as settlement velocity and brand composition have shifted. A stable incentive rate under real transaction load is evidence of deliberate policy management — relevant for brands assessing whether a verified commerce network can maintain consistent data economics at scale.
